statement.text: Conjecture Let $C$ be a Cantor set embedded in $\mathbb{R}^n$. Is there a self-homeomorphism $f$ of $\mathbb{R}^n$ for every $\epsilon$ greater than $0$ so that $f$ moves every point by less than $\epsilon$ and $f(C)$ does not intersect $C$? Such an embedded Cantor set for which no such $f$ exists (for some $\epsilon$ ) is called "sticky". For what dimensions $n$ do sticky Cantor sets exist?

title: Sticky Cantor sets
